subject: Mechanical Engineering
title: Mobile Robots: Warehouses on Wheels
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Mobile Robots: Warehouses on Wheels.

hook.text: Amazon warehouses use thousands of orange robots that slide under shelves, lift them, and carry them to workers.

buildup.text: AGVs follow painted lines or magnetic strips. AMRs use lidar and cameras to navigate freely without tracks.

discovery.text: A fleet controller assigns tasks and routes to hundreds of robots simultaneously, preventing collisions and jams.

twist.text: The robots bring the shelf to the worker — not the worker to the shelf. Walking time drops to nearly zero.

climax.text: Mobile robots doubled Amazon's warehouse throughput while reducing the building footprint. Movement was the bottleneck.

punchline.text: Don't walk to the shelf. Let the shelf walk to you.

quiz.question: How did mobile robots improve Amazon's warehouse efficiency?
options: They replaced all human workers with fully autonomous systems
They bring shelves to workers, nearly eliminating walking time
They sort packages faster by reading barcodes while moving
